title: Constellation Energy Powers AI Growth with Nuclear and Gas Deals
rationale: Constellation's nuclear PPAs with Microsoft, Meta, and CyrusOne directly supply power to AI data centers, benefiting the AI Power & Cooling cohort.
brief_text: Constellation Energy is emerging as a critical player for AI infrastructure by supplying power to data centers. The company signed a 20-year power purchase agreement with Microsoft to restart Three Mile Island, and another 20-year deal with Meta Platforms in June 2025 for nuclear power from the Clinton Clean Energy Center in Illinois, with operations expected to resume in 2027. Its recently acquired unit Calpine also signed a 380-megawatt agreement with CyrusOne for a new data center adjacent to the Freestone Energy Center in Texas, complementing a 400-megawatt deal signed last year. Unlike advanced nuclear reactor companies that face regulatory delays, Constellation's existing nuclear assets can meet AI power demand immediately.

aspects.reason: Calpine, recently acquired by Constellation, signed a 380-megawatt agreement with CyrusOne for a data center.
Signed a 380-megawatt agreement with Calpine for a new data center adjacent to Freestone Energy Center.

title: Vertiv Stock Jumps 7% on South Korea's $1 Trillion AI and Chip Investment Plan
rationale: Vertiv's power/cooling systems benefit from $356B Korean AI DC investment; 20% Asia sales.
brief_text: Vertiv shares surged 7% after South Korea announced a government-corporate plan to invest more than $1 trillion in semiconductor fabrication plants and AI data centers. Corporate spending accounts for the bulk, with Samsung and SK Hynix investing about $518 billion in new chip plants, while SK Group, GS Group, and Naver will invest about $356 billion in AI data centers. Vertiv, which generates about 20% of its sales in Asia and has a presence in South Korea, is seen as a key beneficiary of AI data center buildouts because its power systems infrastructure is embedded in Nvidia's architecture. Naver is a key partner of Nvidia, further linking Vertiv to the spending plans.

title: AI data center expansion drives utilities to sign multi-gigawatt power deals
rationale: AI power demand surge directly benefits power & cooling equipment providers as data centers expand.
brief_text: Utilities are securing multi-year electricity supply agreements with data center operators as AI infrastructure buildout accelerates power demand. Alliant Energy disclosed five fully executed data center agreements totaling approximately 3.4 gigawatts, including a new 370-megawatt electric service agreement with a ramp targeted by the end of 2030. PowerBank Corporation signed a modular data center joint development agreement with Nodiac.ai, pairing solar and battery storage systems with a co-location model to bypass grid interconnection timelines. Both regulated utilities and independent power producers, spanning fuel cells, nuclear, natural gas, and renewables, are positioning to serve this load growth, with thematic ETFs such as the Defiance AI & Power Infrastructure ETF and the Global X Data Center & Digital Infrastructure ETF offering exposure.

aspects.reason: Nodiac.ai entered a joint development agreement with PowerBank Corporation for modular data centers, driving demand for its data center services.

title: Ford pivots to data center energy storage with new subsidiary Ford Energy
rationale: Ford's entry into utility-scale battery storage for AI data centers increases supply of power/cooling solutions, benefiting the node.
brief_text: Ford Motor Company is launching Ford Energy, a wholly owned subsidiary that will manufacture utility-scale battery energy storage systems for AI data centers, repurposing its electric vehicle battery manufacturing footprint. The move follows a $19.5 billion write-down of its EV programs last year and comes as data center operators face power shortages. Ford will spend $2 billion to retool its Glendale, Kentucky, facility—originally a multibillion-dollar EV battery joint venture with South Korea’s SK On—to produce the Ford Energy DC Block, a 5.45-megawatt-hour containerized grid storage system using lithium iron phosphate chemistry. The company has entered a five-year framework deal with EDF Power Solutions that could be worth up to $4 billion if all options are exercised, and it aims to manufacture and deploy 20 gigawatt-hours of energy storage capacity annually, with first shipments expected as soon as 2027.

aspects.reason: EDF Power Solutions enters a five-year framework deal with Ford Energy worth up to $4 billion.

title: Analog Devices Reports Record AI Revenue and Acquires Empower Semiconductor
rationale: ADI's record AI demand and Empower acquisition strengthen power-management supply for AI DCs.
brief_text: Analog Devices reported record-setting revenue driven by strong demand from AI data centers and industrial customers, alongside an agreement to acquire Empower Semiconductor to deepen its AI-focused power-management capabilities. Management disclosed that it had previously been shipping more than 10% below end-market consumption in key segments, highlighting a reservoir of pent-up demand now starting to flow through its results. The Empower Semiconductor acquisition directly expands Analog Devices' power-management offerings for AI data centers at a time when that business is already a key growth driver. Combined with record quarterly revenue and strong margins, this reinforces the idea that AI infrastructure could be a meaningful earnings engine, but it also heightens investors' exposure to swings in AI-related capital spending as a short term risk.

title: Big Tech’s $3 Trillion Struggle to Secure Enough Electricity
rationale: Power & cooling demand surges as Big Tech races to secure electricity; long-term deals and new capacity needed.
brief_text: Big Tech is facing a critical shortage of electricity to power AI data centers, with utilities quoting two- to four-year wait times just for feasibility studies. Global data center power demand could rise 165% by the end of the decade, according to Goldman Sachs. Companies like Amazon, Microsoft, and Google are racing to lock in long-term power deals, such as Amazon’s agreement with Talen Energy for up to 1,920 megawatts of nuclear power and Microsoft’s 20-year deal with Constellation Energy to restart Three Mile Island for 835 megawatts. Bitzero, which controls over a gigawatt of clean power capacity across Norway, Finland, and North Dakota, has already secured a 15-year lease with OneQode Networks for its full 110-megawatt Norway campus, potentially generating $2.6 billion in contracted revenue. Shark Tank’s Kevin O’Leary is a strategic investor, noting that Bitzero’s sustainable, low-cost electricity positions it as a power provider in an era where AI and Bitcoin mining compete for the same resource.

title: Vertiv Stock Jumps 7% on South Korea's $1 Trillion AI and Chip Investment Plan
rationale: South Korea's $356B AI data center plan boosts demand for Vertiv's power/cooling systems.
brief_text: Vertiv shares surged 7% by midday after South Korea announced a government-corporate plan to invest more than $1 trillion in semiconductor fabrication plants and AI data centers. Corporate spending accounts for the bulk of the plan, with Samsung and SK Hynix investing about $518 billion in new chip fabrication plants, while SK Group, GS Group, and Naver will invest about $356 billion in AI data centers. Vertiv, which generates about 20% of its sales in Asia and has an active presence in South Korea, is well-positioned to benefit from the AI data center buildout due to its power systems infrastructure technology and its partnership with Nvidia. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has described Naver as a key partner in the global AI ecosystem, and Vertiv's power systems are embedded in Nvidia's architecture, leading to optimism that Vertiv will see increased orders from this spending wave.

title: Bitzero signs $2.6 billion AI power lease deal in Norway
rationale: Growing data center electricity demand (945 TWh by 2030) drives need for power/cooling equipment.
brief_text: Bitzero has signed a binding letter of intent for a 15-year lease covering the full 110 megawatt capacity of its Namsskogan, Norway data center site with OneQode Networks, marking its formal entry into large-scale AI data-center infrastructure. The agreement carries an implied value of roughly $2.6 billion over the lease term and could generate approximately $176 million to $178 million in annual revenue at full utilization. Bitzero, which has secured more than a gigawatt of low-cost power across Norway, Finland, and the United States, is transitioning from low-carbon bitcoin mining to providing power for the data-center industry. The company's Norway operations already run bitcoin mining at power costs below four cents per kilowatt-hour, and an additional 70-megawatt tranche at Namsskogan is scheduled for energization in the fourth quarter of 2026. Global data center electricity demand is projected to approach 945 terawatt-hours by 2030, and securing power has become a critical bottleneck, with more than 70% of interconnection requests withdrawn.

title: Pembina Approves C$4.6 Billion Greenlight Power Project for AI Data Centers
rationale: Combined cycle turbines (Siemens Energy) for AI data center power & cooling.
brief_text: Pembina Pipeline Corporation has approved the final investment decision for the Greenlight Electricity Center, a major energy infrastructure project in Alberta's Industrial Heartland. The project, developed with Morgan Stanley Infrastructure Partners and Kineticor Asset Management, will supply dedicated electricity to a hyperscale data center under a long-term tolling agreement, with commercial operations expected in the second half of 2030. Total project expenditures are estimated at roughly C$4.6 billion, with Pembina's net investment at approximately C$2.1 billion after land sale proceeds. The facility will use combined cycle technology featuring Siemens Energy turbines and has expansion permits for up to about 1,864 megawatts. Pembina expects its ownership interest to generate around C$310 million in annual run-rate adjusted EBITDA once operational.

title: AI Infrastructure Buildout Shifts Focus to Energy as Scarce Resource
rationale: Power constraints drive demand for efficient cooling and power equipment; critical for AI DCs.
brief_text: Trillions of dollars are being poured into AI factories, but the scarcest resource is energy, not chips or models. McKinsey estimates AI-related infrastructure spending could exceed $5 trillion by 2030, while JLL projects developers may require roughly 100 gigawatts of new data-center capacity over the same period. Utilities face multi-year waits for grid connections, forcing companies like Microsoft, Google, and Amazon to secure dedicated power. Bitzero, which controls a development pipeline exceeding one gigawatt of potential capacity across Norway, Finland, and North Dakota, announced a binding letter with OneQode Networks for a 15-year lease on the full 110 megawatts of its Namsskogan campus, valued at approximately $2.6 billion. Kevin O'Leary, a key backer, said he considers Bitzero a real estate power company with sub-six cents per kilowatt-hour power, land, permits, and water, adding that perhaps 50 percent or more of announced U.S. data centers won't be built due to lack of grid power.

aspects.reason: Bitzero announced a binding 15-year lease for 110 MW of its Namsskogan campus valued at $2.6 billion, indicating strong demand for its data center capacity.

title: Bitzero secures 110 MW Norway lease with OneQode as AI power crunch deepens
rationale: Power shortage drives demand for efficient cooling and power infrastructure; Bitzero's low-cost power underscores need.

The company controls over one gigawatt of potential capacity across Norway, Finland, and North Dakota, with power costs as low as three to four cents per kilowatt-hour, roughly 70 percent below the U.S. average. Bitzero is already cash flow positive from Bitcoin mining, with an all-in breakeven around $50,000 per coin, well below the industry average of $75,000 to $82,000. Strategic investor Kevin O'Leary has called the company 'really a power company,' highlighting its early-mover advantage in securing cheap, sustainable electricity before the current grid crisis. While tech giants like Microsoft and Google target 2028 or later for new nuclear capacity, Bitzero's Norway site is expected to begin deployment by early 2027.

title: SpaceX Acquires xAI and Cursor for $60 Billion to Build AI Infrastructure
rationale: Orbital AI servers with space radiators and solar power drive demand for advanced cooling and power solutions.
brief_text: SpaceX has acquired xAI and Cursor in a $60 billion deal to accelerate its artificial intelligence infrastructure business. The company is building large AI data centers and plans to deploy orbital AI servers powered by continuous solar energy, cooled by space radiators, and connected via Starlink. This vertical integration mirrors Amazon's path from e-commerce to AWS, positioning SpaceX as a core provider for the AI economy. The acquisitions bring advanced model development and developer tools in-house, creating a closed-loop system between AI software and hardware.

title: Analog Devices buys Empower Semiconductor amid record AI-driven revenue
rationale: ADI's acquisition of Empower adds high-density power tech for data centers, benefiting AI power & cooling node.
brief_text: Analog Devices reported record revenue driven by demand from AI data centers and industrial customers, and announced an agreement to acquire Empower Semiconductor to expand its AI power management capabilities. The stock last closed at $386.91, with year-to-date returns of 41.3%. The acquisition adds high-density power technology that can increase Analog Devices' content in data-center systems, tightening the link between its core analog and mixed-signal franchises and power delivery for advanced processors. Management flagged that gross margins could come under pressure as factories run near full capacity, which may limit operational leverage if volume keeps rising.

title: Nextpower to Acquire Prevalon Energy for Up to $365 Million
rationale: Prevalon's BESS for data-center power competes with existing power/cooling providers, but magnitude is weak as it's one player's move.
brief_text: Nextpower announced a definitive agreement to acquire battery energy storage systems provider Prevalon Energy for up to $365 million. The deal expands Nextpower beyond solar tracking into energy storage, energy management software, and critical power infrastructure for utility grids, AI data centers, and industrial power systems. Prevalon has deployed more than 6 GWh of BESS systems globally and holds 1.3 GW of firm supply contracts supporting AI and hyperscaler data-center infrastructure. Nextpower also raised its fiscal 2027 revenue outlook to a range of $4.0 billion to $4.4 billion, up from the prior $3.8 billion to $4.1 billion. RBC Capital maintained an Outperform rating on Nextpower and increased its price target to $149 from $146, citing the acquisition's fit with the company's inverter business.

aspects.reason: Prevalon Energy is being acquired by Nextpower for up to $365M, implying a positive outcome for its owners.

title: Bitzero signs $2.6 billion AI hosting lease with OneQode for Norway data center
rationale: New data center buildout increases demand for power and cooling equipment.
brief_text: Bitzero has signed a binding letter of intent with Singapore-based OneQode for a 15-year, 110-megawatt lease at its Norway data center site, expected to generate approximately $2.6 billion in total contracted revenue over the life of the agreement. The deal covers the full initial capacity of Bitzero's flagship facility in Namsskogan, with OneQode planning a large-scale GPU deployment rolled out in phases and initial commissioning targeted for the first half of 2027. Bitzero, which operates as a licensed grid operator at the 132-kilovolt level in Norway, owns its high-voltage feed lines and substations, giving it an all-in electricity cost of just 4.3 cents per kilowatt-hour—roughly half what most major data center operators pay. The company expects an 85 percent site net operating income margin on the lease, implying approximately $151 million in annual net operating income at full capacity, while Bitcoin mining continues to generate cash flow during the buildout. A definitive lease agreement is expected within 60 to 90 days, and Bitzero plans to finance the estimated $1.1 billion buildout through debt, with late-stage discussions already underway with multiple banks.

title: Tesla, Sunrun, Renew Home Form Coalition to Deliver Over 16GW of Flexible Energy Capacity
rationale: Alternative to traditional power/cooling solutions may reduce demand for dedicated infra.
brief_text: Tesla, Sunrun, and Renew Home have formed a coalition to deliver over 16 gigawatts of flexible energy capacity to help meet surging electricity demand from data centers and AI growth. The companies aim to aggregate existing home batteries, solar systems, and smart thermostats into a virtual power plant that could provide more than 16GW of flexible capacity. This framework creates essential grid headroom by optimizing existing transmission and distribution capacity, and can be deployed in months, offering a significantly faster alternative to building traditional large-scale power facilities. Homeowners can earn rewards and reduce energy bills through grid-supporting programs, while hyperscalers and utilities gain a unified, scalable resource to navigate grid congestion and accelerate data center operations.

title: Chevron Just Jumped Ahead of ExxonMobil in Capturing This Massive Opportunity
rationale: Increased natural gas power for data centers may drive demand for cooling and power equipment.
brief_text: Chevron has taken an early lead over ExxonMobil in the race to supply dedicated natural gas power for AI data centers. Chevron announced a partnership with Microsoft and power developer Engine No. 1 to develop projects that could eventually supply up to 4 gigawatts of electricity to U.S. data centers, with the first facilities expected online by 2028. ExxonMobil, meanwhile, has partnered with NextEra Energy to market an initial 1.2 gigawatt natural gas power project with carbon capture, but it is still seeking customers. The Electric Power Research Institute estimates data centers could consume 9% to 17% of all U.S. electricity by 2030, up from about 4% to 5% today, creating a new market for energy infrastructure providers.

title: UBS Raises Bloom Energy Price Target to $350 on Expanded Brookfield Partnership
rationale: Bloom Energy's fuel cells provide reliable onsite power for AI data centers, bypassing grid constraints; strong demand and backlog signal positive supply-side impact.
brief_text: UBS raised its price target on Bloom Energy shares to $350 while maintaining a Buy rating, driven by Brookfield Asset Management's expansion of its committed funding framework to $25 billion, a five-fold increase since the original partnership in October 2025. The move signals growing institutional confidence in Bloom Energy's role as a critical infrastructure provider for AI data centers, with the company's solid oxide fuel cell technology offering reliable onsite power that bypasses strained electrical grids. Bloom Energy's first-quarter sales surged 130% year-over-year to $751 million, and management raised full-year guidance to at least $3.4 billion, supported by a $20 billion total backlog and major partnerships with Oracle, Nebius, and Brookfield. Evercore ISI also raised its target to $350 with an Outperform rating, while Clear Street increased its target to $290 but maintained a Hold due to valuation concerns, and BMO Capital reiterated a Market Perform rating with a $279 target, cautioning that the Brookfield commitment is a programmatic financing framework rather than confirmed immediate backlog. Bloom Energy stock currently trades at about 39 times sales and over 210 times forward earnings, with a consensus Moderate Buy rating and a mean price target near $259, signaling potential downside from current levels.

title: GE Vernova jumps 7.3% on Russell Top 50 inclusion and AI power orders
rationale: Rising orders for power generation and grid equipment from AI data centers directly benefit GEV's cohort.
brief_text: GE Vernova shares rose 7.3% after the company was added to the Russell Top 50 Index and reported rising orders for power generation and grid equipment from AI-driven data centers. The index inclusion is expected to boost visibility with institutional investors, while the AI-related infrastructure demand highlights the importance of its gas turbine, grid, and electrification businesses. A recent 2.5-gigawatt gas and nuclear collaboration with Blue Energy in Texas ties directly into the AI power buildout. However, the company still faces execution risks from its loss-making Wind segment and potential European project delays.

aspects.reason: Blue Energy's 2.5 GW gas and nuclear collaboration with GE Vernova ties into AI power buildout, indicating demand for its energy projects.

title: Nike, ServiceNow, Constellation Brands among stocks making biggest premarket moves
rationale: Bloom Energy partnership with Brookfield to finance AI infrastructure power projects.
brief_text: Nike fell more than 3% premarket after reporting a 12% sales decline in Greater China, despite beating earnings and revenue estimates for its fiscal fourth quarter. Constellation Brands rose about 1.5% after posting first-quarter earnings of $3.43 per share, above the $3.20 consensus, with revenue also topping expectations and full-year guidance roughly in line. Shutterstock plunged more than 30% and Getty Images dropped 4% after Getty called off their proposed merger due to demands from a U.K. regulator. Alcoa declined 4% after announcing a $4.1 billion deal to acquire South32's bauxite, alumina and aluminum portfolio. ServiceNow gained more than 5% and Salesforce nearly 4% after Guggenheim upgraded both to buy, citing attractive valuations and dismissing AI as a threat. Bloom Energy jumped over 7.5% on an expanded partnership with Brookfield to finance power for AI infrastructure projects. Kroger slipped 2% after agreeing to acquire Giant Eagle for $1.65 billion. Sandisk tumbled 3.5% and Micron Technology fell about 2.5% on the first trading day of the third quarter, following more than tripling in the prior quarter.

title: Europe Data Center Construction Market to Reach $58.74 Billion by 2031
rationale: Rising AI/HPC workloads drive adoption of liquid cooling in European data centers, benefiting cooling providers.
brief_text: The Europe data center construction market is forecast to grow from $16.99 billion in 2025 to $58.74 billion by 2031, at a compound annual growth rate of 22.96%. Rising AI and high-performance computing workloads are driving adoption of liquid cooling technologies such as direct-to-chip and immersion cooling, with companies like Spode Works Regeneration Ltd planning new facilities featuring these advanced techniques. Hyperscale data centers lead investment, supported by expansions from Google in Germany and other major players, while Western Europe, particularly the FLAP-D market, dominates regional spending. The UK holds the largest power capacity, followed by the Nordics, which attract investment due to their renewable energy sources. Key infrastructure providers include ABB, Schneider Electric, and Siemens, with major investors such as AWS, Digital Realty, and Equinix fueling market growth.

title: Vertiv Holdings Completes ThermoKey Acquisition, Expands Thermal-Management Portfolio
rationale: Vertiv's acquisitions of ThermoKey and CoolIT's cold plate breakthrough strengthen its thermal management for AI data centers, benefiting the AI Power & Cooling cohort.
brief_text: Vertiv Holdings has completed its acquisition of ThermoKey, expanding its thermal-management portfolio across Europe, the Middle East, and Africa to support high-end AI computing. The deal brings over 30 years of engineering experience and technology that complements Vertiv's existing offerings, giving customers flexibility to optimize for performance and growth. Bernstein initiated coverage on Vertiv with an Outperform rating and a $416 price target, citing its position as a pure-play data center infrastructure stock with robust earnings power. GLJ Research upgraded Vertiv from Sell to Hold, noting that CoolIT's 15kW cold plate breakthrough adds viability to Vertiv's single-phase cooling offering beyond the 2030s. Vertiv was recently added to the S&P 500 index and has surpassed earnings estimates for three consecutive years.

title: Amazon could become first company to hit $1 trillion in annual revenue by 2028, analyst says
rationale: Massive capex implies huge power/cooling demand for AI data centers.
brief_text: Amazon could become the first company to generate $1 trillion in annual revenue by 2028, according to Futurum Equities Chief Market Strategist Shay Boloor. Boloor said the projection is supported by Amazon's increasingly diversified business model, which spans commerce, cloud, logistics, advertising, and artificial intelligence. Amazon plans to invest about $200 billion in capital expenditures in 2026, supported by major customer commitments including more than $100 billion from OpenAI. Its custom chip business has surpassed a $20 billion annualized revenue run rate and is growing at triple-digit rates. In April, Amazon reported first-quarter revenue of $181.52 billion, topping Wall Street estimates of $177.30 billion, and earnings of $2.78 per share, well above the consensus forecast of $1.66 per share.

title: Vertiv Boosts Data Center Portfolio Through Acquisitions, Expects Strong Q2 Revenue Growth
rationale: Vertiv's acquisitions strengthen its thermal/cooling portfolio, benefiting the AI Power & Cooling cohort via enhanced capabilities and market share.
brief_text: Vertiv is strengthening its data center infrastructure portfolio through recent acquisitions including PurgeRite, ThermoKey, BMarko Structures, and Strategic Thermal Labs, which contributed 4% to revenues in the first quarter of 2026. The company completed its acquisition of ThermoKey, enhancing its thermal management and heat-exchange capabilities, while the PurgeRite deal deepens fluid management services for liquid-cooled deployments. Vertiv also acquired BMarko to expand structural fabrication and manufacturing capacity, broadening its end-to-end offering. For the second quarter of 2026, Vertiv expects revenues between $3.25 billion and $3.45 billion, with organic net sales growth in the 20-24% range. The company faces increasing competition from Super Micro Computer and Amphenol in AI infrastructure, though its shares have surged 89.5% year-to-date, and the Zacks Consensus Estimate for 2026 earnings is $6.36 per share, up 3.41% over the past 30 days.

title: Tesla Could Become a Space Stock Through Deep Ties With SpaceX
rationale: SpaceX and xAI are major buyers of Tesla's Megapacks for data centers and moonbase, boosting demand for AI power & cooling.
brief_text: Tesla may increasingly be viewed as a space stock due to its close ties with SpaceX, which just completed an IPO raising around $86 billion with another $25 billion expected via a bond issuance. SpaceX’s IPO prospectus mentions Tesla more than 80 times, highlighting that SpaceX and its xAI segment are major buyers of Tesla’s Megapacks for data centers and a planned moonbase. The companies are also partnering on the Terafab chip manufacturing initiative and co-developing Macrohard, an AI agentic platform that could eventually run from orbital data centers. While Tesla is not yet a pure space stock, its hardware and software could increasingly be launched into orbit.

title: NextEra Energy or Vistra: Which Utility Stock Wins the AI Power Supercycle?
rationale: AI data center boom drives surging electricity demand, benefiting power and cooling providers like Vistra and NextEra.
brief_text: NextEra Energy and Vistra are positioned to benefit from surging electricity demand driven by the artificial intelligence data center boom, but Vistra may offer greater upside potential. NextEra, with its $67 billion all-stock acquisition of Dominion Energy, aims to create the world's largest regulated electric utility with over 10 million customers and 110 gigawatts of generation capacity, heavily betting on AI power demand in data center hubs like Northern Virginia. Vistra, an integrated power producer and retailer serving about five million customers, is seen as a direct AI play due to its large natural gas and nuclear fleet, including the second-largest nuclear fleet in the U.S., and its pending $4 billion acquisition of Cogentrix to expand its natural gas footprint. Vistra recently signed two 20-year power purchase agreements with hyperscalers Meta and Amazon Web Services, locking in long-term revenue. On valuation, Vistra trades at a forward price-to-earnings ratio of 17.9 times and a price-to-sales ratio of 3.3 times, compared to NextEra's 21.3 times and 6.6 times, respectively. While NextEra offers stability and dividend growth, its high debt load from the Dominion deal in a high-interest-rate environment may limit upside, making Vistra the preferred pick for investors willing to accept additional risk.

title: Data center construction boom draws electricians and HVAC techs away from home projects, causing delays and higher costs
rationale: HVAC technicians are pulled to data center jobs, indicating strong demand for cooling equipment and installation services.
brief_text: The surge in data center construction is pulling skilled electricians and HVAC technicians away from residential work, leading to longer wait times and higher prices for homeowners. Data center construction starts hit $25.2 billion in early 2025, with spending surpassing $50 billion for the first time in April, now accounting for 2.3% of all U.S. construction spending. Electrical work can represent 45% to 70% of a data center project's budget, and workers can earn 25% to 30% more on these jobs, according to a Wall Street Journal report. In Abilene, Texas, homebuilder Gene Lantrip said his subcontractors are losing crews to a massive AI data center campus backed by Oracle and OpenAI, adding two months to project timelines. In Scottsdale, Arizona, wait times for AC repairs have stretched from two days to five or six days, and a panel upgrade that cost $3,500 two years ago now runs $4,200.

title: VoltServer and Eaton Form Strategic Partnership to Advance Next-Generation Power Distribution
rationale: Partnership develops next-gen power distribution for AI data centers, improving supply of power/cooling solutions.
brief_text: VoltServer and Eaton have formed a strategic partnership to advance next-generation power distribution infrastructure. The collaboration includes a strategic investment by Eaton in VoltServer and will focus on developing intelligent, integrated, end-to-end power systems by combining Eaton's power management portfolio with VoltServer's Digital Electricity platform and fault-managed power expertise. The companies aim to address growing demand from AI, edge computing, and electrification by enabling safe power delivery over longer distances, reducing installation complexity, and improving operational flexibility. Initial development efforts will target hardware and software solutions for environments where digital infrastructure resiliency, efficiency, and speed of deployment are critical.

aspects.reason: VoltServer receives strategic investment from Eaton and partnership to commercialize its Digital Electricity platform.

title: 中东数据中心建设市场预计2031年达113.8亿美元
rationale: Liquid cooling adoption rising from 41% to 54% by 2031 to support AI workloads, boosting cooling equipment demand.
brief_text: 中东数据中心建设市场预计将从2025年的28.7亿美元增长至2031年的113.8亿美元，复合年增长率为25.79%。人工智能计划的推进推动了对AI就绪数据中心的需求，例如Khazna Data Centers于2025年4月在土耳其安卡拉附近启动了一个大型AI就绪项目。液冷技术的采用率预计将从2025年的41%上升至2031年的54%，以支持日益增长的AI工作负载。然而，2025年6月以色列与伊朗的冲突等地缘政治紧张局势已导致投资暂停和扩张放缓，2026年3月的一次攻击影响了亚马逊云服务和甲骨文在阿联酋和巴林的设施。沙特阿拉伯预计到2031年将引领市场，而伊拉克、约旦和黎巴嫩等新兴市场则提供了成本优势机会。

aspects.reason: Khazna Data Centers于2025年4月在土耳其安卡拉附近启动大型AI就绪项目

title: Navitas Semiconductor Outpaces Nvidia and Broadcom in 2026
rationale: Navitas' new power-efficiency solution for AI data centers directly benefits the AI Power & Cooling cohort by improving efficiency.
brief_text: Navitas Semiconductor has surged past Nvidia and Broadcom in 2026, driven by a new power-efficiency solution for AI data centers. In March, the company introduced a DC-DC power delivery board that converts 800 volts to 6 volts in a single stage, targeting Nvidia AI infrastructure. Morgan Stanley raised its price target to $12.50 from $4.20 in May, while Baird lifted its target to $20 from $9. The stock now trades at 92 times sales, far above its five-year average of 11.8.

title: China data center market to reach $101.47 billion by 2031
rationale: New green standards mandate PUE ≤1.4 and up to 100% renewable energy by 2032, driving power/cooling upgrades.
brief_text: The China data center market is projected to grow from an estimated $60.69 billion in 2025 to $101.47 billion by 2031, at a compound annual growth rate of 8.94%. Government initiatives are boosting local GPU production amid export constraints, while Alibaba Group announced a new AI inferencing chip in September 2025. The AI Plus initiative is driving AI adoption across research, public services, and finance. Joint ventures are expanding digital capacity, with Nyocor planning facilities in Xinjiang to host over 100,000 AI chips. Chindata Group secured over $490 million to enhance digital infrastructure, and new green standards mandate a power usage effectiveness not exceeding 1.4, with renewable energy usage reaching up to 100% by 2032.

aspects.reason: Chindata Group secured over $490 million to enhance digital infrastructure

title: Fermi America selects TSK for engineering and project management of Project Matador phase two in Texas
rationale: Gas turbines and power infrastructure for AI data centers; positive for power & cooling equipment.
brief_text: Fermi America has selected Spanish EPC contractor TSK to lead engineering and project management for the second phase of Project Matador, a massive Texas power campus. TSK will oversee permitting and infrastructure planning for three Siemens SGT6-5000F gas turbines intended to provide reliable, dispatchable power for the site. Project Matador is a private energy system designed to supply up to 17 gigawatts of electricity directly to hyperscale AI and advanced computing facilities, combining natural gas, nuclear, solar, and battery storage to meet surging technology sector energy demands. The partnership reflects a growing trend of developers investing in dedicated power assets to secure electricity for AI infrastructure, with Fermi aiming to accelerate development timelines and reduce execution risks by leveraging TSK's specialized EPC expertise.

aspects.reason: TSK was selected for engineering and project management of Project Matador phase two.

title: FuelCell Energy upgraded to Buy at B. Riley as data center deal boosts investment case
rationale: FuelCell Energy's 380MW order for data center power deployment indicates growing demand for alternative power solutions for AI data centers.
brief_text: FuelCell Energy shares surged 25.8% on Monday after the Export-Import Bank of the United States agreed to a $49 million financing package for the company and B. Riley turned bullish, upgrading the stock to Buy from Neutral. Analyst Ryan Pfingst raised the price target to $32 from $13, citing increased confidence from a firm order with Fit Energy USA for as much as 380 megawatts of power deployment for data centers. The agreement is with Fit Energy USA, an energy infrastructure developer focused on fuel cell technology and natural gas turbines, backed by private investment firm Fit Ventures. Pfingst also forecast positive EBITDA generation for FuelCell Energy starting in the second half of 2027.

title: Fermi Selects TSK to Advance Engineering for Texas Power Project
rationale: Gas turbines and power infrastructure for AI data centers; increases demand for power/cooling equipment.
brief_text: Fermi America has selected Spanish EPC contractor TSK to provide early works engineering and project management services for three Siemens SGT6-5000F gas turbines that will anchor the second phase of its Project Matador development in Texas. Under the agreement, TSK will carry out engineering and management work to advance permitting, support site mobilization, and oversee the Siemens contract-related engineering scope, aiming to shorten development timelines and reduce execution risk. Project Matador is Fermi America's flagship behind-the-meter power campus designed to supply electricity directly to hyperscale AI and advanced computing facilities, with plans for up to 17 GW through combined-cycle natural gas, nuclear, grid, solar, and battery storage. The three turbines are expected to provide dispatchable generation while longer-term infrastructure is built out, reflecting a broader trend of dedicated power assets for surging AI-driven electricity demand.

title: Bitzero Signs $2.6 Billion AI Data-Center Lease in Norway
rationale: New data center build-out implies increased demand for power/cooling equipment, but magnitude is low as it's one site.
brief_text: Bitzero Holdings has signed a binding letter of intent with OneQode Networks to lease the full 110-megawatt capacity of its Namsskogan, Norway data center site for 15 years, marking its entry into large-scale AI infrastructure. The deal carries an implied value of roughly $2.6 billion over the lease term and could generate annual revenue of $176 million to $178 million at full utilization. Bitzero, which also has a one-gigawatt development campus in Finland and a North Dakota site in the United States, will earn recurring infrastructure revenue while OneQode pays the electricity costs for GPU-based AI workloads. The company continues to mine Bitcoin using low-cost power secured across Norway, Finland, and the U.S., and counts Shark Tank's Kevin O'Leary as a strategic investor.

title: GLJ Research Upgrades Vertiv Holdings to Hold
rationale: Vertiv's acquisition of ThermoKey strengthens its thermal management portfolio, positively impacting the AI Power & Cooling node.
brief_text: GLJ Research analyst Austin Wang upgraded Vertiv Holdings Co to Hold from Sell on June 18. The upgrade follows Vertiv's June 12 completion of its acquisition of ThermoKey, which expands its thermal management portfolio and manufacturing capacity across Europe, the Middle East, and Africa. CEO Giordano Albertazzi stated that rising AI infrastructure deployments have made thermal performance critical, and that ThermoKey enhances Vertiv's ability to deliver integrated heat rejection solutions. ThermoKey CEO Giuseppe Visentini added that the deal combines the company's heat-exchange expertise with Vertiv's integrated thermal platform, preserving engineering operations in Italy and supporting future growth.

aspects.reason: ThermoKey's heat-exchange expertise is combined with Vertiv's integrated thermal platform, preserving engineering operations and supporting future growth.

title: Willdan Group Highlights Data Center Cooling and Grid Services in Investor Presentation
rationale: Willdan provides cooling optimization services, competing indirectly with hardware cooling vendors; effect on the cohort is weak and ambiguous.
brief_text: Willdan Group released its June investor presentation, detailing how its consulting, engineering, and implementation services address data center cooling and grid planning. The company works on mission-critical campuses, offering engineering, energy assessments, controls integration, procurement, and construction management. It cited an Evoque Data Centers project that achieved 1.5 million kilowatt-hours of annual savings through cooling system optimization, setpoint adjustments, and improved controls. Willdan's exposure to the thermal-management problem in AI data centers comes from its work in energy efficiency, utility interconnection, load forecasting, and facility systems rather than direct liquid-cooling hardware.

aspects.reason: Evoque Data Centers is mentioned as a client project achieving energy savings, reflecting successful engagement with Willdan.

title: Emerald Wealth Partners Says Oracle’s AI-Driven Backlog Surge Makes Stock Irrationally Cheap
brief_text: Emerald Wealth Partners, in its first-quarter 2026 Growth Equity Strategy investor letter, argued that Oracle Corporation’s stock is irrationally undervalued after its remaining performance obligation jumped from $104 billion to $523 billion in the second half of 2025, driven by AI training contracts including a notable deal with OpenAI. The firm noted that Oracle now trades below its pre-announcement level, implying the market assigns negative or zero value to the massive additional backlog, which consists of non-cancelable contracts. While acknowledging that Oracle will take on approximately $80 to $100 billion in new debt for AI data center investments, Emerald Wealth Partners believes the expanded business opportunities and large margin of safety more than compensate for the increased risk. The letter also highlighted that the $248 billion in data center capacity contracted over 15 to 19 years could be sub-leased to hyperscalers like Microsoft in any excess capacity scenario, given the chronic shortage of powered data center space. Oracle shares closed at $142.50 on July 1, 2026, with a market capitalization of $410.47 billion, and have lost nearly 40% over the past 52 weeks.

title: Unitree Technology IPO Registration Approved, Humanoid Robot Concept Active
brief_text: The China Securities Regulatory Commission has approved Unitree Technology's registration application for an initial public offering and listing on the STAR Market, with a target fundraising amount of 4.202 billion yuan. The funds raised will be invested in intelligent robot research and development and manufacturing base construction. The news boosted the humanoid robot concept in the A-share market, with Kailong High-Tech hitting the 20 percent daily limit up and Shoukai Shares hitting the 10 percent daily limit up. At the industry level, Tesla's Optimus robot production line at the Fremont factory has entered a critical mass production stage, and UBTECH has launched its full-size ultra-bionic humanoid robot U World U1 series, with cumulative online and offline orders exceeding 13,361 units. Analysts believe that the upstream core component sector has stronger development certainty and will benefit first.

title: PPL sees 28.3 GW in advanced data center projects, raises Kentucky load forecast
brief_text: PPL Corporation disclosed that data center projects in advanced planning stages reached 28.3 gigawatts in the first quarter of 2026, up 12% sequentially from 25.2 gigawatts, with nearly 10 gigawatts under signed Electric Service Agreements and about 5 gigawatts already under construction. In Kentucky, projected load growth through 2032 increased to 12.9 gigawatts from the previous 8.5 gigawatts, supported by interest from 13 new data center projects representing nearly 12 gigawatts of potential demand. Global Laser Enrichment and Toyota Motor Manufacturing announced combined investments of $2.6 billion in PPL's service territory, prompting management to raise expected new load to 3.5 gigawatts by 2032 from 1.8 gigawatts. To support this growth, PPL plans to invest about $23 billion through 2029, driving 10.3% annual rate base growth and upper-end 6-8% EPS growth.

aspects.reason: Global Laser Enrichment announced $2.6 billion investment in PPL's territory, indicating demand for PPL's services

title: Banks get creative as AI-fueled corporate debt soars
brief_text: As corporate borrowing tied to artificial intelligence shows no sign of slowing, bankers are coming up with new ways to sell ever larger volumes of debt. Large technology companies known as hyperscalers, such as Amazon and Alphabet, have issued $60 billion in bonds in multiple currencies over the last 12 months to tap a wider pool of investors and prevent saturation in the U.S. market. Amazon raised €14.5 billion in March from an eight-part deal, the largest ever in the euro corporate bond market, while Alphabet set borrowing records in yen, Canadian dollars, Swiss francs, and sterling. Capital expenditures for hyperscalers this year are estimated at around $725 billion, nearly double the level seen in mid‑2025, and spending is rising faster than operating cash flow, creating the need for external funding. Bankers are also structuring deals around pre-arranged data center leases to provide more visibility on future cash flows, with about 15 such deals sold to high-yield investors since last year, including an $810 million note issued by Stingray Compute that was nine times oversubscribed. Despite the surge in supply, demand remains strong, though some investors question whether the market can continue to absorb the volume, with Morgan Stanley estimating AI debt could push investment-grade issuance above $2 trillion for the first time ever in 2026.

title: Berkshire Hathaway triples Alphabet stake despite double-digit stock decline
brief_text: Berkshire Hathaway, now led by CEO Greg Abel, more than tripled its stake in Alphabet, making it the conglomerate's fifth-largest holding, even as the stock fell by double digits in recent weeks. The decline followed Alphabet's guidance for $180 billion to $190 billion in 2026 capital expenditures, an $80 billion private placement to fund AI infrastructure, and the departures of AI leaders Noam Shazeer to OpenAI and Nobel laureate John Jumper to Anthropic. Abel led a $10 billion investment in the private placement, signaling confidence in Alphabet's AI spending, while Warren Buffett's long-held view is that stock declines are buying opportunities. Alphabet continues to report record cloud backlog and revenue growth, with CFO Anat Ashkenazi citing unprecedented AI demand.

title: Tech Equity Sales Renew AI Debt-Binge Worries
brief_text: A surge in equity sales by major technology companies is raising concerns among bond investors about an impending wave of debt issuance to fund artificial intelligence spending. This month alone, Alphabet Inc. sold $85 billion in shares and SpaceX completed a record $75 billion initial public offering, with OpenAI and Meta Platforms Inc. also considering equity raises. While equity bolsters balance sheets, investors like Tom Murphy of Columbia Threadneedle warn it signals heavier capital expenditure and more borrowing ahead. JPMorgan Chase & Co. now forecasts $5.5 trillion in AI and data center spending through 2030, up $400 billion from its November estimate, and expects $2.1 trillion in high-grade bond financing over five years. SpaceX's $25 billion bond deal weakened sharply in secondary trading, with paper losses reaching about $360 million, and Alphabet's bonds also softened after its equity announcement. Some money managers view the equity sales positively, but others caution that equity is supplementing rather than replacing debt, potentially forcing issuers to pay higher spreads.

title: Analog Devices Reports Record AI Revenue and Acquires Empower Semiconductor
brief_text: Analog Devices reported record-setting revenue driven by strong demand from AI data centers and industrial customers, alongside an agreement to acquire Empower Semiconductor to deepen its AI-focused power-management capabilities. Management disclosed that it had previously been shipping more than 10% below end-market consumption in key segments, highlighting a reservoir of pent-up demand now starting to flow through its results. The Empower Semiconductor acquisition directly expands Analog Devices' power-management offerings for AI data centers at a time when that business is already a key growth driver. Combined with record quarterly revenue and strong margins, this reinforces the idea that AI infrastructure could be a meaningful earnings engine, but it also heightens investors' exposure to swings in AI-related capital spending as a short term risk.

title: Analog Devices buys Empower Semiconductor amid record AI-driven revenue
brief_text: Analog Devices reported record revenue driven by demand from AI data centers and industrial customers, and announced an agreement to acquire Empower Semiconductor to expand its AI power management capabilities. The stock last closed at $386.91, with year-to-date returns of 41.3%. The acquisition adds high-density power technology that can increase Analog Devices' content in data-center systems, tightening the link between its core analog and mixed-signal franchises and power delivery for advanced processors. Management flagged that gross margins could come under pressure as factories run near full capacity, which may limit operational leverage if volume keeps rising.

title: Apple Eyes Foldable iPhone Production Boost
brief_text: Apple is reportedly planning at least five new iPhone models between the second half of 2026 and the first half of 2027 as it prepares for a larger product cycle. The company has asked suppliers to prepare for about 10 million foldable iPhones, up from an earlier plan of 7 million to 8 million units. Apple also has secured components for about 80 million smartphones across new models planned for the second half of 2026. Total smartphone production for 2026 is expected to exceed 220 million units, giving the company stronger purchasing power as AI-driven demand tightens memory chip supply. Apple is also reportedly in talks to source memory chips for China-sold devices from Chinese suppliers, including ChangXin Memory Technologies and Yangtze Memory Technologies, though the company has not confirmed those discussions.

aspects.reason: Apple is in talks to source memory chips from YMTC for China-sold devices, potentially increasing demand for YMTC's products.

title: Hut 8 Shifts From Bitcoin Mining to Data Center Business, Analyst Sees 4% Upside
brief_text: Hut 8 has strategically shifted its focus from bitcoin mining toward high-performance computing and AI infrastructure. Rosenblatt Securities analyst Chris Brendler maintained a Buy rating on the stock with a $124 price target, implying about 4% upside from current levels. The company's subsidiary Beacon Point DC recently raised $4.25 billion through a private debt offering carrying a 6.129% interest rate and maturing in 2042. Hut 8 operates across four segments—Digital Infrastructure, Power, Compute, and Others—and aims to build its energy and technology infrastructure business for the long term.

title: Navitas Semiconductor Outpaces Nvidia and Broadcom in 2026
brief_text: Navitas Semiconductor has surged past Nvidia and Broadcom in 2026, driven by a new power-efficiency solution for AI data centers. In March, the company introduced a DC-DC power delivery board that converts 800 volts to 6 volts in a single stage, targeting Nvidia AI infrastructure. Morgan Stanley raised its price target to $12.50 from $4.20 in May, while Baird lifted its target to $20 from $9. The stock now trades at 92 times sales, far above its five-year average of 11.8.

title: Soitec and ZenSemi partner on 300mm BCD-on-SOI production
brief_text: Soitec and ZenSemi have announced a strategic collaboration to enable high-volume production of 300mm BCD-on-SOI technologies for next-generation power electronics. Soitec will supply its advanced 300mm Power-SOI substrates to support ZenSemi’s development and capacity ramp-up of a new BCD-on-SOI process, targeting applications such as AI datacenters, electric vehicles, humanoid robots, and industrial systems. The partnership aims to provide fabless companies and integrated device manufacturers with a high-performance manufacturing platform, leveraging Soitec’s engineered substrate expertise and ZenSemi’s specialty foundry capabilities. ZenSemi reported successful first-silicon validation with a lead customer, achieving a roughly 30% die size reduction for an 18-channel analog front-end device compared to traditional bulk BCD processes. The companies plan to rapidly scale 300mm SOI-BCD manufacturing capacity to serve both domestic Chinese design houses and global clients.

aspects.reason: ZenSemi achieved first-silicon validation with a lead customer, demonstrating a 30% die size reduction for its BCD-on-SOI process.

title: Oracle Stock Drops on Report OpenAI May Delay IPO to 2027
brief_text: Oracle shares fell 2.58% on June 26 after a New York Times report that OpenAI is considering postponing its initial public offering until 2027. The decline reflects investor concern over Oracle’s deep infrastructure ties to OpenAI, as the delayed IPO could force Oracle to carry massive, unmonetized data center outlays on its balance sheet without the near-term commercial windfall a public listing would provide. Oracle has staked much of its growth narrative on being the cloud backbone for premier AI entities, but the deferred timeline signals broader friction in the AI landscape and fears that enterprise demand may not scale fast enough to justify the pace of Oracle’s buildout. Despite the drop, Wall Street maintains a consensus Strong Buy rating on Oracle with a mean price target of about $259, implying nearly 75% upside from current levels.

title: HIVE Digital upsizes note to $115 million to fuel AI and GPU cloud expansion
brief_text: HIVE Digital Technologies has upsized its zero-coupon exchangeable note offering to US$115 million to accelerate its AI infrastructure, GPU cloud, and high-performance computing ambitions. The financing, originally launched at US$100 million, provides low-cost capital to support the company's scaling strategy, with proceeds earmarked for future GPU acquisitions, including a recent agreement with Cohere involving around 2,300 NVIDIA GPUs and another significant GPU opportunity in the pipeline. The funds will also help convert HIVE's Boden, Sweden facility into a Tier III HPC data centre, with municipal approval to purchase the land marking a major milestone. CEO Aydin Kilic emphasized the strong demand for compute, noting that long-term HPC contracts offer stable cash flows compared to the cyclical nature of crypto mining.

title: Chinese Hedge Funds Warn AI ‘Super Bubble’ Is Ready to Burst
brief_text: Two of China's best-known hedge fund managers are warning that the artificial intelligence boom in global stock markets has become an unsustainable bubble. Wealspring Asset, whose founder Yang Dong is well-known in China for calling the top in 2007, said global AI stocks have become a 'super bubble' and that the 'collapse point may not be far away,' according to an investor letter seen by Bloomberg News. Shanghai Banxia Investment Management Center said 'the trigger for the AI bubble to burst has already appeared,' citing pressure on breakneck revenue growth at Anthropic PBC. At least four other Chinese hedge funds expressed reluctance around AI in May, according to a monthly summary of fund views compiled by CSC Financial Co. and seen by Bloomberg News, while four funds in the summary were positive and the remaining seven didn't give a stance on AI. Wealspring, which manages more than $1.4 billion of assets, wrote that many of China's AI infrastructure companies lack a long-term moat, run 'quite ordinary' business models, and require constant capital spending to sustain their growth, adding that some of the hottest shares in China's domestic stock market were 'very likely' to crash more than 80%. Banxia, which manages more than $294 million, predicted that Anthropic's annualized revenue run-rate will fall short of market expectations and that large tech companies will recoil at the rising cost of tokens while competitors may chip away at its popularity among computer programmers.

title: Mid-Size Passenger Cars Lead Demand in Vehicle Communication Protocols
brief_text: The global automotive communication protocol market is projected to grow from USD 7.77 billion in 2026 to USD 10.32 billion by 2033, at a CAGR of 4.1%. Mid-size passenger cars are forecasted to be the largest vehicle class throughout the period, dominating global production and sales and integrating advanced safety, infotainment, and connectivity solutions that necessitate higher network node counts. Automotive Ethernet is poised for rapid growth due to its capability to handle high-bandwidth data transmission essential for ADAS and infotainment, with prominent OEMs like Volkswagen, BMW, and General Motors adopting Ethernet-centric architectures. The North American market, particularly the US, is projected to experience significant growth, driven by extensive integration of safety and infotainment network nodes and the presence of semiconductor giants such as Texas Instruments and Microchip Technology. Key players in the market include NXP Semiconductors, Robert Bosch GmbH, Infineon Technologies AG, and STMicroelectronics.

aspects.reason: Bosch is listed as a key player in the automotive communication protocol market, which is projected to grow.

title: Kandi Technologies’ subsidiary Xinchu New Energy named authorized distributor of Schneider Electric
brief_text: Kandi Technologies announced that its subsidiary Xinchu New Energy has been named an authorized distributor by Schneider Electric for fiscal year 2026. The authorization allows Xinchu to distribute and support Schneider Electric’s APC, MGE, and Schneider-branded portfolio, including uninterruptible power supply systems, cooling infrastructure, racks, cabinets, software, and related technical services. This strengthens Xinchu’s ability to deliver integrated power infrastructure solutions for data centers, telecommunications base stations, and energy storage systems. Kandi believes the authorization marks an important milestone in expanding its upstream hardware capabilities and supply chain foundation for the AI data center backup power and energy storage market. By combining Schneider Electric’s proven UPS and data center infrastructure portfolio with Xinchu’s proprietary energy storage batteries and Battery Management System technologies, Xinchu can offer integrated, one-stop power solutions for both backup power and energy storage applications.

title: Anthropic Could Become the Most Valuable Software Company in History
rationale: Anthropic's IPO and cloud/TPU spending with Google may boost demand for general compute processors, but effect on cohort is weak as it's one customer.
brief_text: Anthropic has confidentially filed for an initial public offering, potentially becoming the largest software IPO in history after a recent funding round valued the company at $965 billion. Amazon has invested approximately $13 billion to date with plans for up to $20 billion more, and its stake could now exceed $100 billion. Alphabet owns an estimated 14% stake worth roughly $135 billion, and Anthropic has committed to spending $200 billion on Google's cloud services and TPU chips over five years. Salesforce has built a stake worth approximately $5 billion, while Nvidia and Microsoft have also invested up to $10 billion and $5 billion respectively, forming equity-tied relationships with the AI company.

title: Micron briefly surpasses Meta and Tesla in market value amid AI memory boom
rationale: AI-fueled supply crunch for DRAM/NAND/HBM drives revenue and ASP growth for memory cohort.
brief_text: Micron briefly surpassed the market valuations of Meta and Tesla for the first time on Thursday before settling back to nearly match them on Friday, closing with a market cap near $1.27 trillion. The Boise-based memory chip maker has seen its stock soar over 236% in the past month to $1,132 a share, driven by an AI-fueled supply crunch for DRAM and NAND memory, particularly High-Bandwidth Memory. Third-quarter revenue quadrupled year-over-year to $41.45 billion, with profits jumping from $1.88 billion to $28.2 billion, and the company forecast fourth-quarter revenue between $49 billion and $51 billion. Micron has signed 16 long-term strategic customer agreements across data center, consumer, and auto segments, including with Nvidia and AI lab Anthropic, which it says will fundamentally transform its business model. Analysts like William Blair’s Sebastien Naji reiterated an Outperform rating, citing continued average selling price growth and improving revenue visibility from these agreements.

title: Tim Cook Calls the Memory Crisis a 'Hundred-Year Flood'
rationale: Memory suppliers benefit from surging prices; Micron's gross margins rose to 84.9%.
brief_text: Apple announced price hikes across its MacBook and iPad lineup, its first formal move to pass higher memory and storage costs on to consumers, with increases ranging from $100 to $300. CEO Tim Cook told the Wall Street Journal it was a 'hundred-year flood,' and the company said it has never seen a component price increase this much, this quickly, leaving the door open to further increases. Memory and storage prices have quadrupled in the past three quarters, according to Counterpoint Research, as suppliers redirect production toward high-bandwidth memory used in AI servers. Micron reported gross margins of 84.9% in its most recent quarter, up from 39% a year ago, surpassing Nvidia and Meta. Counterpoint estimates the higher component costs could add roughly $200 per iPhone for Apple, with price increases of $150 to $200 expected across the lineup, while IDC expects all new iPhone models to move to 12GB of RAM as Apple pushes Apple Intelligence features that require more memory, and sees Apple's average selling price rising 12% this year.

title: Minden Electronics' subsidiary GMC Microelectronics raises wafer foundry prices by 10% to 20%, plans 1 billion yuan private placement
rationale: Power semi foundry price hike 10-20% and silicon wafer price hike 15% indicate tightening supply and pricing power for the Analog, Power & Discrete cohort.
brief_text: Minden Electronics disclosed that, benefiting from a reversal in the supply-demand dynamics of the power semiconductor industry and tightening capacity at mature-node wafer foundries, its controlled wafer foundry GMC Microelectronics will raise foundry prices by 10% to 20% starting June 2026. Its equity-participated silicon wafer company Jingrui Electronics will also follow with a 15% price hike from July 1. The core product monthly sales volume of the company's controlled design house Guangwei Integration has jumped from about 1,000 wafers in early 2025 to over 10,000 wafers currently. The company also disclosed a targeted fundraising plan, intending to raise 1 billion yuan, of which 700 million yuan will be used for a specialty high-voltage power semiconductor devices and power integrated circuit wafer foundry project, and 300 million yuan to replenish working capital and repay bank loans. GMC Microelectronics' first-phase production facility is planned for a monthly capacity of 100,000 six-inch silicon-based wafers. Currently, both capacity and orders are full, and the company is advancing full production for the first phase through various channels while preparing to start second-phase construction at an appropriate time. Jingrui Electronics is operating at full production and full sales. It has completed about 200 million yuan in equity financing this year and built a new monocrystalline ingot project, which is expected to commence production by the end of this year or early next year.

title: Micron's 4.4x Revenue Surge Confirms Memory Supercycle, Roundhill ETF Offers Sub-$100 Entry
rationale: Memory supercycle with tight supply and long-term contracts benefits DRAM/NAND/HBM cohort.
brief_text: Micron Technology's fiscal 2026 third-quarter revenue surged 4.4 times year over year to $41.4 billion, with earnings per share jumping 13 times to $25.11, reinforcing that the memory supercycle is sustainable. Management expects tight memory supply to persist beyond 2027, and customers are signing long-term contracts to secure supply. The Roundhill Memory ETF, trading just over $60, allows investors with less than $100 to gain exposure to global memory leaders including Samsung, SK Hynix, Sandisk, and Kioxia, alongside Micron. The ETF has already appreciated 118% in three months since its April launch. Market research firm TrendForce projects the global memory market will generate $889.3 billion in revenue this year and $1.28 trillion next year, indicating further growth potential.

title: State Council Approves the '15th Five-Year Plan' for Building a Sports Powerhouse, Advancing the Development of the 'Three Major Ball Sports'
rationale: ASML raised revenue guidance due to sustained AI-driven demand for advanced lithography equipment.
brief_text: The State Council has approved the '15th Five-Year Plan' for building a sports powerhouse, calling for improvements to the public service system for national fitness, reforms to the competitive sports management system, strengthened youth sports programs, and the revitalization and development of the 'three major ball sports'—football, basketball, and volleyball. Lithography giant ASML has raised its full-year revenue guidance, primarily driven by sustained demand for advanced lithography equipment related to AI chip manufacturing. The China Securities Regulatory Commission has approved the registration application of Unitree Technology for its initial public offering and listing on the STAR Market. The company's humanoid robot shipments in 2025 have already exceeded 5,500 units, ranking first globally in the industry. CSPC Pharmaceutical's holding subsidiary, Jushi Biotech, has signed an agreement with AstraZeneca to carry out strategic cooperation in the field of novel small interfering RNA drug candidates. AstraZeneca will make an upfront payment of 30 million US dollars, with potential milestone payments of up to 1.74 billion US dollars. BOE Technology Group saw a net institutional seat purchase of 1.458 billion yuan, while China Resources Microelectronics' order backlog reached a new high.
